records.name: ASAP Chess (After School Activities Partnerships)
records.summary: The chess program of ASAP, a Philadelphia nonprofit for after-school activities. It helps schools, libraries and rec centers run weekly chess clubs for kids, then sends the players to a school league and free citywide tournaments.
records.what_you_do: Kids play chess each week at a club in their school or library. Players can then compete in the school league (October to February) or in the free monthly Saturday tournaments (October to May).

schedule.text: Weekly club meetings during the school year at partner schools, libraries and rec centers. The Scholastic League runs October through February. Free Saturday tournaments run monthly from October through May.

locations.label: Partner schools, libraries and rec centers citywide

cost.text: Saturday tournaments are free and open to the public. Club fees were not listed on the pages we read, so ask the school or site.

first_step.how: Ask your child's school, library or rec center whether it runs an ASAP chess club. Families can also use the program locator on the ASAP site or email chess@phillyasap.org.
first_step.basis: Clubs are open through schools and sites, and ASAP lists a way to ask, but the joining path runs through each site rather than a walk-in sign-up.

records.notes: Counts disagree between sources. The ASAP chess page says more than 150 clubs and over 2,500 students, with no year shown. A January 2026 Chalkbeat article says about 1,000 students play chess with ASAP. We used the chess page for the program description and Chalkbeat for the 2026 sign of life. The office address and phone come from the ASAP homepage; verify before printing. The Saturday tournament dates on the site (Nov 7 and Dec 5) show no year. The league contact is named on the chess page and was not recorded here. Free Saturday tournaments are open to the public even though the clubs run through schools, which is why open_to is students. A Blackwell library Saturday club (3:30 to 4:45 pm, undated) is listed in leads_only. ASAP also runs a Scrabble program, recorded separately as ASAP Scrabble Clubs.

records.name: ASAP Scrabble Clubs
records.summary: The Scrabble program of ASAP, a Philadelphia nonprofit for after-school activities. Kids meet each week in school and library clubs to play Scrabble, and the program recently launched a citywide school league.
records.what_you_do: Players meet weekly in a school or library club to play word games, and can take part in citywide events and the Philadelphia Scholastic Scrabble League.

schedule.text: Weekly play in school and library clubs during the school year. The league dates were not listed on the pages we read.

locations.label: Partner schools, libraries and rec centers citywide

cost.text: Club fees were not listed on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Ask your school or library whether it has an ASAP Scrabble club, or start one through the Start a club page on the ASAP site.
first_step.basis: The program runs through schools and sites with a listed way to start a club, but the page gives no Scrabble-specific sign-up steps.

records.notes: Same nonprofit as ASAP Chess, listed separately because it is a different club network. The programs page gives more than 80 clubs and 1,500 students, with no year shown; not checked against a second source. The Chalkbeat article from January 2026 says ASAP supports Scrabble clubs at schools, libraries and rec centers. The board_games tag is the closest fit in the cheat sheet.

records.name: Philly Mah-Jawn Mahjong Club
records.summary: A Philadelphia mahjong club that meets every week for players of all levels. It has a clubhouse in Old City, teaches newcomers, and its president said in August 2026 that weekly crowds had grown to about 50 people.
records.what_you_do: Learn to play mahjong, including the Japanese riichi style, join the weekly play, and take part in club tournaments.

schedule.text: Meets weekly. The 2026 news reports did not give a day or time. The August 2026 report says the weekly meetups happen at board game cafes, and the club also has a clubhouse at 2nd and Chestnut Streets in Old City.

locations.label: Board game cafes (weekly meetups, per August 2026 report)

cost.text: Dues and drop-in costs were not stated in the sources we read.

first_step.how: Go to a weekly meetup and ask for a lesson, or check the club's website for how to join.
first_step.basis: A May 2026 news report says newcomers are welcome, lessons are held, and volunteers teach first-time visitors at meetups.

records.notes: The club's own website loaded but gave only its name to our reader, so the day, time, dues and join steps are not confirmed. Dates come from WPVI (6abc) reports dated May 13, 2026 and August 6, 2026. The August report says the club has been active since 2019 and opened an Old City space in 2025. A Billy Penn piece mentions a Philadelphia Riichi Open hosted by the club on Nov 8 and 9, but its year was not shown, so it is not recorded. Mahjong has no exact tag, so it is filed under board_games as the closest fit.

records.name: Philly Pinball Club
records.summary: A Monday night pinball league at Barcade Fishtown. Players sign up at the venue, play four games a night, and compete through a season that ends with finals. A newcomer's first night is free.
records.what_you_do: Sign up when you arrive, play four pinball games each Monday, and compete through the season toward the finals. The club also runs off-season tournaments.

schedule.text: Mondays at Barcade Fishtown. Sign-ups start at 7:30 pm and games at 8 pm. Seasons run through the year, with about eight weeks of play and a finals night. The summer 2026 season ran July 27 to September 28.

cost.text: $20 for the season, paid by Venmo or cash. A newcomer's first night is free.

first_step.how: Go to Barcade Fishtown on a Monday, with sign-ups from 7:30 pm. Your first night is free.
first_step.basis: The club's newsletter says newcomers get a free first night and gives a fixed sign-up time, so a new player knows how to start.

records.notes: The club's own newsletter is the source and runs through the Sept 28, 2026 finals. No fall 2026 dates were posted as of Oct 8, 2026; the fall 2025 season started Sept 15, 2025. The Barcade Fishtown street address was not shown on the venue pages we read, so it is left blank. Pinball has no exact tag, so it is filed under video_games. The venue's age policy was not checked.

records.name: Belles and Chimes Philly
records.summary: A women's pinball league that meets at Barcade Fishtown on the second Tuesday of each month. Players sign up at the venue and play league nights, plus occasional tournaments.
records.what_you_do: Sign up on the league sheet at the venue, play monthly league nights, and enter the group's tournaments, which have included summer, spooky season and winter events.

schedule.text: Second Tuesday of each month at Barcade Fishtown. Sign-ups begin around 7:30 pm and games start shortly after 8 pm.

cost.text: The newsletter posts we read do not give a price for league nights.

first_step.how: Go to Barcade Fishtown on the second Tuesday and sign up on the league sheet from about 7:30 pm. The newsletter has a subscribe form for news.
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up on league night, but the posts do not describe a welcome or first-timer help for newcomers.

records.notes: The newest post is dated January 13, 2026. Posts from October 2025, November 2025 and January 2026 all match the second-Tuesday pattern. No spring to fall 2026 league posts were in the archive we read, so confirm the next league night before going. The Barcade Fishtown street address was not shown, so it is left blank. The women's focus is stated in the newsletter as women's pinball leagues.

records.name: IGDA Philly
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the International Game Developers Association. It holds free monthly meetings where local game makers give talks, with networking time first. Meetings are in person at Drexel or online.
records.what_you_do: Attend a free monthly meeting with 30 minutes of networking, then talks by local developers. Join the chapter's Discord to hear about upcoming meetings.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings. The May 2026 meeting ran from 7 to 9 pm, with networking first and talks from 7:30. Meetings are in person at Drexel University's URBN Center or online by Zoom.

first_step.how: Register for the online webinar through the chapter's registration link, or RSVP in the chapter's Discord for in-person meetings.
first_step.basis: Meetings are free and open, with a published way to register, but the chapter does not describe a newcomer or beginner program.

records.notes: The chapter page gives news by month only. The newest dated event we found is May 12, 2026, and no later 2026 meeting was posted when we looked. Online registration uses the bit.ly link on the event page (http://bit.ly/IGDAPhillyMonthlyReg). The chapter page links to national IGDA membership; its cost was not checked. The homepage does not give a meeting day, so the day is not recorded.

records.name: Philcon
records.summary: A science fiction, fantasy and horror convention run by the Philadelphia Science Fiction Society, a nonprofit. It turns 90 in 2026 and depends on volunteers to staff its art show, stage tech, registration, gaming room and con suite.
records.what_you_do: Before the convention, volunteers help with publicity, social media, program planning or proofreading. During the convention, volunteers staff registration, run stage tech, load equipment in and out, and help with the art show, masquerade, green room, con suite and gaming room.

schedule.text: Annual convention, Friday to Sunday, November 20 to 22, 2026, at the DoubleTree by Hilton in Cherry Hill, New Jersey. Volunteer load-in starts the Thursday before.

locations.label: DoubleTree by Hilton, Cherry Hill, NJ
locations.address: 2349 Marlton Pike West, Cherry Hill, NJ

cost.text: Membership prices were not checked. Volunteers can earn a rollover membership for next year after 12 volunteer hours.

first_step.how: Email volunteers@philcon.org with what you would like to help with, or stop by the convention office during the event.
first_step.basis: Anyone can ask to volunteer by email or at the office, but the volunteer page does not say whether experience is needed.

records.notes: Cherry Hill is across the river in New Jersey, so in_city is false. The volunteer page does not list dates, so the 2026 dates come from the homepage. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian signature on the liability release. The site's footer names the Philadelphia Science Fiction Society as a 501(c)(3). The volunteer page's age rule covers under-18s only; there is no stated adult minimum.

records.name: Zenkaikon
records.summary: An all-volunteer anime and fan convention held in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. It was founded in 2006 by merging two Philadelphia-area conventions.

locations.label: Lancaster County Convention Center, Lancaster, PA

records.notes: Held in Lancaster, well outside the city, so it does not meet just outside Philadelphia. Founded in 2006 by merging Kosaikon (Villanova) and Zentrancon (Penn). The next event on the site is March 18 to 21, 2027. Its volunteer staff is all-volunteer. Re-check if a Philadelphia chapter or city-based volunteer program forms.

notes: Second sweep for games-puzzles, after the existing records (Queen and Rook, Chess Club at South Philadelphia Library, Redcap's Corner and others were not re-checked). Searches: 10 of 10 used, cap reached. Fetches: 36. Records: 8 (7 publish, 1 out_of_area). GAPS: (1) Bridge: no Philadelphia duplicate club found in search. The ACBL club directory refused our fetch, so this lane is empty and needs a run with directory access. (2) Go: only Penn Go Society, from a Meetup page; its own domain did not resolve. (3) Free Library game clubs (D&D, chess, mahjong, Magic, board game clubs) have 2026 listings in search summaries, but the calendar refused every fetch, so they are in leads_only, not records. A later run with calendar access should check them. (4) Chess: ASAP is the main provider. MasterMinds Chess Club (founded 2001 per a roughly 2019 article in search) has no website or URL found, so it is not written. Franklin Mercantile Chess Club did not appear in any search. (5) Scrabble: ASAP Scrabble recorded; the Delco club is outside the city. (6) Puzzle hunts, escape rooms and Mahjong: no standing weekly puzzle-hunt team found. Eric the Puzzler runs monthly and seasonal street hunts and a weekly online word puzzle, none of which is a joinable group, so not recorded. (7) Game development: IGDA Philly recorded; Philly Game Forge and Philly Dev Night were not found. (8) Fandom conventions: Philcon recorded (Cherry Hill, NJ, in_city false). Zenkaikon is out of area (Lancaster). Fan Expo Philadelphia is a commercial show, not a group, so not recorded. (9) Magic and Pokemon leagues: no store's own site confirmed a weekly league, so those stores are in leads_only. (10) Pinball: Philly Pinball Club and Belles and Chimes Philly recorded. Mahjong and pinball have no exact tags in the cheat sheet, so they use the closest tags (board_games, video_games). OTHER FINDINGS: ASAP's own site and Chalkbeat disagree on club and student counts; both are in the ASAP Chess notes. The Barcade Fishtown street address was not visible on the Barcade pages we could read, so both pinball records leave the address blank. Idealist and PACDC job pages, the Philly Mah-Jawn club's /events and /about pages, and the Penn Go Society website returned 404 or did not resolve, so no facts were taken from them. Plain-language check: no dashes used as punctuation.
